pages.title: How to choose a graphics card for your PC
pages.description: Choose a GPU around your games, monitor and exact card dimensions. Understand VRAM, benchmark settings, power connections and total upgrade cost.
pages.answer: Start with your games and monitor, then check comparable game tests and the dimensions of the exact card. A GPU chip name, memory capacity or generated-frame headline cannot answer all three questions.
sectionTitles: Set a useful target before shopping
Read benchmarks with their settings attached
Treat VRAM as capacity, not a performance score
Check the complete card and power path
Compare the whole upgrade cost

pages.title: How to choose a processor without overlooking the platform
pages.description: Compare CPUs for your games and applications, then check motherboard support, BIOS, memory, cooling and the complete platform upgrade cost.
pages.answer: Choose a CPU for the work you need it to do, then price and verify the whole platform. Core count and boost clock are useful specifications, but neither replaces application tests or the motherboard support list.
sectionTitles: Separate a new build from an upgrade
Understand cores, clocks and cache
Verify motherboard support before ordering
Budget for memory and cooling
Make the upgrade decision measurable

pages.title: How to choose PC memory: capacity, DDR generation and timings
pages.description: Understand RAM capacity, DDR4 and DDR5 compatibility, kit configuration, transfer rates and CAS latency before choosing a memory upgrade.
pages.answer: Match the memory generation and physical module type first. Choose capacity for your workload, then compare supported kits and timings. A lower CL number only has meaning alongside its transfer rate.
sectionTitles: Identify the platform before the kit
Use workload evidence to choose capacity
Compare transfer rate and latency together
Check the installation and supported profile
Keep a matched kit and a useful checklist

pages.title: How to choose an SSD: capacity, interface and motherboard fit
pages.description: Choose an SSD by capacity, SATA or NVMe interface, M.2 size and motherboard support. Understand speed claims, endurance and storage units.
pages.answer: Choose enough capacity, then verify the drive’s interface and physical format against your motherboard. M.2 describes the shape; it does not by itself establish SATA or NVMe support.
sectionTitles: Plan capacity around the files you keep
Match the interface and physical format
Read the slot notes, not just the slot count
Interpret speed and endurance honestly
Understand the capacity shown by software

pages.title: RTX 5070 vs RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB: memory, power and buying checks
pages.description: Compare RTX 5070 and RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB specifications, understand the VRAM tradeoff, and check exact card fit and benchmark settings before buying.
pages.answer: The RTX 5070 has more CUDA cores but 12 GB of memory; the RTX 5060 Ti variant here has 16 GB and a lower reference power rating. Use game tests and the exact local listing to make the purchase decision.
sectionTitles: More memory and more rendering resources answer different questions
Keep native FPS separate from generated frames
Check the card you will actually order

pages.title: RTX 5070 vs RX 9070: specifications and upgrade checks
pages.description: Compare GeForce RTX 5070 and Radeon RX 9070 memory and power specifications. Check game testing, application support and exact partner-card fit.
pages.answer: The RX 9070 specification lists 16 GB of memory and 220 W typical board power; the RTX 5070 lists 12 GB and 250 W total graphics power. These differences help plan an upgrade, but do not establish a universal game or application winner.
sectionTitles: Use evidence from the workloads you run
Check feature and software requirements separately
Make the purchase comparison about exact models

pages.title: Ryzen 7 9800X3D vs 7800X3D: specifications and platform checks
pages.description: Compare AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D and 7800X3D architecture, clocks and AM5 requirements. Check BIOS and total upgrade cost before changing your CPU.
pages.answer: Both processors use AM5 and have 8 cores, 16 threads and 96 MB of L3 cache. The 9800X3D uses Zen 5 with higher published clocks. Check workload tests and exact motherboard BIOS support before deciding whether an upgrade is worthwhile.
sectionTitles: What the specifications establish
What an AM5 upgrade still needs
New build and existing-owner decisions differ

pages.title: AM5 CPU upgrade checklist: BIOS, memory, cooling and storage
pages.description: Plan an AM5 CPU upgrade with an exact motherboard support-list check, BIOS notes, memory configuration, cooler mounts and storage lane checks.
pages.answer: An AM5 socket match starts the check; it does not finish it. Confirm the exact CPU on the board support list, the required BIOS, the cooler mount, memory configuration and any slot-sharing rules before buying.
sectionTitles: Record the system you have
Make CPU support a documented check
Check memory and cooling as configurations
Review expansion and storage notes
Keep a final verification record

pages.title: RAM latency calculator: compare MT/s and CAS timing
pages.description: Calculate first-word CAS latency in nanoseconds from memory transfer rate and CL. Compare two kits with transparent formulas and clear limitations.
pages.answer: Enter a kit’s transfer rate in MT/s and CAS latency in cycles. The calculator returns CL × 2,000 ÷ MT/s in nanoseconds. It compares one timing component, not total memory latency or game FPS.

pages.title: SSD capacity planner: storage budget and TB to GiB conversion
pages.description: Plan SSD capacity for games, applications and files. Convert advertised decimal TB to binary GiB and set your own free-space allowance.
pages.answer: Enter the advertised drive capacity and the storage you expect to use. The tool converts decimal TB to binary GiB, adds your workload budget and reserves the free-space percentage you choose.
